summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic headaches, hypertension, diabetes, and hyperaldosteronism was admitted due to a four-day worsening headache and a prior episode of substernal chest pressure. She presented after a clinic visit revealed severely elevated blood pressure (217/126 mmHg) and papilledema, leading to transfer from the nephrology clinic to the emergency department. Initial management included IV labetalol and hydralazine, which reduced her blood pressure. Cardiac workup, including serial troponins and EKGs, showed no evidence of myocardial infarction; chest pain was attributed to GERD given her history and normal cardiac testing. A CT head showed no hemorrhage or mass effect, with stable white matter changes. Blood pressure was stabilized with increased oral labetalol, and headache improved. She was discharged home in good condition with medication adjustments, including labetalol three times daily and a short course of oxycodone/acetaminophen for headache, along with smoking cessation counseling.
